name: Voice Fundamental Frequency
description: Analyzes voice F0 (fundamental frequency) patterns — voice cloning often has unnatural F0 contours.
mechanism:
This method analyzes voice fundamental frequency (F0) for deepfake detection:

1. **F0 Extraction**: The fundamental frequency (pitch) of the voice is extracted per frame using autocorrelation, cepstral, or YIN algorithm. F0 corresponds to the vocal fold vibration rate, typically 85-180 Hz for males and 165-255 Hz for females.

2. **F0 Contour Analysis**: The temporal F0 contour (pitch track) is analyzed for naturalness. Natural speech shows characteristic F0 patterns: (a) declination (gradual F0 decrease across utterances), (b) prosodic contours (rises for questions, falls for statements), (c) micro-prosody (F0 perturbations at phoneme boundaries). AI voice synthesis may produce F0 contours with incorrect prosodic patterns or missing micro-prosodic detail.

3. **F0 Range and Variability**: Each speaker has a characteristic F0 range and variability. The method checks whether F0 statistics (mean, standard deviation, range) fall within physiologically plausible values for the apparent speaker. AI-generated voices may show either unnaturally constrained (monotone) or excessive F0 variability.

4. **Jitter and Shimmer**: Natural voice shows slight cycle-to-cycle F0 variation (jitter, typically <1%) and amplitude variation (shimmer, typically <3%). These micro-perturbations reflect the biomechanics of vocal fold vibration. AI voice synthesis may produce either too-perfect (zero jitter/shimmer) or incorrectly modeled perturbation patterns.

5. **F0-Visual Correlation**: Voice F0 should correlate with visible physical effort — higher pitch may correspond with increased tension visible in the neck muscles. The method checks audio-visual F0 correspondence. Deepfakes combining generated audio with generated video may show poor F0-visual correlation.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
